# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Meridian Health Plan — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Riley Hayes
Member ID: W842220872
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-18 — Reference number POC-A0C827A88A-54850 — ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888**

**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines, https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), which Meridian Health Plan issued on 2026-08-18 under reference number POC-A0C827A88A-54850. The notice states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records already in the plan's possession line up with the plan's own published criteria. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I set out the plan's criteria in the plan's own words and show where my records meet them.

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

**1. No severe arthritis, and no X-ray required where the MRI shows no significant arthritis.**

The policy states:

> "ACL reconstruction or repair may be medically necessary when the criteria in any of the following sections are met and individual has no evidence of severe arthritis defined as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4"

and:

> "If the MRI results demonstrate an ACL tear and there is no mention of significant arthritis, especially in the younger individual, X-rays are not required. However, in others with significant MRI evidence of arthritis, standing X-rays are required to confirm that no Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 changes are present"

My MRI of the knee on 2026-06-22 shows a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern, menisci intact, and no significant arthritis. Because the MRI demonstrates an ACL tear with no mention of significant arthritis, the plan's own language says standing X-rays are not required in my situation, and there is no evidence of Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 changes in my records.

I would also note that the first sentence above requires the criteria in **any** of the following sections to be met — not all of them.

**2. History of instability.**

The policy states:

> "Patient history of instability at the time of an acute injury or history of recurrent knee instability (as defined subjectively as 'giving way', 'giving out', 'buckling', two-fist sign)"

My records document recurrent instability with pivoting, and that my knee has given way twice on stairs.

**3. Physical examination findings.**

The policy states:

> "Physical examination findings demonstrate a positive Lachman test, Lachman test 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A, 3B, anterior drawer, pivot shift test, or instrumented (KT- 1000 or KT-2000) laxity of greater than 3 mm side-side difference"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side. The summary available to me does not name each individual test by name; the specific tests performed and their results are recorded in my surgeon's examination note [office note of Dr. Duval, MD — date]. I am asking that this note be obtained and reviewed before any further determination is made, and my surgeon's office can provide it on request.

**4. Clinical correlation.**

The policy states:

> "There is clinical correlation of the individual’s subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)"

My subjective complaints — nine months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, and recurrent instability with pivoting including two episodes of giving way on stairs — correlate directly with the objective MRI finding of a complete mid-substance ACL tear with a bone bruise pattern, and with the positive provocative testing on examination.

**5. Knee pain with documented loss of function.**

The policy states:

> "Knee pain with documented loss of function: Deviation from normal knee function which may include painful weight bearing and/or inadequate range of motion (> 10 degrees flexion contracture or < 110 degrees flexion or both) to accomplish age- appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational or athletic requirements)"

My records document nine months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, range of motion limited by pain, and recurrent instability with pivoting, including giving way twice on stairs. The specific range-of-motion measurements in degrees are recorded in my clinical chart [measured flexion and extension, per office note of Dr. Duval, MD — date]; I am asking that those measurements be reviewed. I would also point out that this criterion is written so that painful weight bearing **or** inadequate range of motion may show the deviation from normal knee function.

**6. Symptom onset, duration, severity, and non-operative management.**

The policy states:

> "Symptom onset, duration, and severity ○ Loss of function and/or limitations ○ Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)"

My records show all of these:

- **Onset and duration:** nine months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Loss of function:** recurrent instability with pivoting, two episodes of giving way on stairs, range of motion limited by pain.
- **Non-operative management:** supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing — 8 weeks, from 2026-05-21 to 2026-07-16, 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-07 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

**7. Timing of injections.**

The policy states:

> "No intra-articular cortisone injections within 4 weeks of surgery (1–3)"

My records document a single corticosteroid injection, given on 2026-05-07 — more than three months before the plan issued this denial on 2026-08-18. Surgery has not yet taken place [scheduled or anticipated surgery date, if known].

**8. Medical stability and absence of infection.**

The policy states:

> "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable"

and:

> "Individual does not have an active local or systemic infection"

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## Request that the plan identify the criteria it applied

The excerpts above are the policy language I have been able to obtain, and several of them plainly introduce further detail I do not have — the criterion beginning "Knee pain with documented loss of function:" and the criterion beginning "Symptom onset, duration, and severity" each introduce lists that are not reproduced in the text available to me, and the sentence "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable" is clearly incomplete as I received it. The policy therefore contains additional conditions that I have not been quoted and cannot address.

The plan holds the criteria that were actually applied to my request. I am requesting, in writing, a copy of the specific clinical review criteria, guideline sections, and any internal rules the reviewer relied on in denying CPT 29888, along with the name and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination. My denial notice states that the determination was made under "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" but does not identify which section of those criteria I failed to meet. Without that, I cannot fully respond, and I ask that it be provided as part of this appeal.

## What I am asking for

I ask Meridian Health Plan to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-18 (reference POC-A0C827A88A-54850) and authorize ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888, as requested by Dr. Duval, MD. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the exact criterion from the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines that my records do not satisfy, and for information about my right to further review, including external review.

Per my denial notice, this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-14**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Please contact me at the phone number and address above if anything further is needed. My surgeon's office can supply the operative planning notes, the MRI report of 2026-06-22, the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-21 to 2026-07-16, and the examination findings referenced above.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Riley Hayes**
Member ID: W842220872
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [List what you send — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-18; MRI report 2026-06-22; physical therapy discharge note; office notes of Dr. Duval, MD]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
